title: Scientists discover breakthrough new way to find alien life with AI | The Independent
body:
The work is reported in a new paper, ‘Chiral discrimination of amino acids in meteorite and desert soil extracts via single-molecule nanogap conductance’, published in the journal Nature Communications.

## Join our commenting forum

Join thought-provoking conversations, follow other Independent readers and see their replies

Comments [...] In the new study, the scientists were able to measure molecules as they passed through a gap between two extremely thin pieces of gold wire. The waveforms of the current as it passes between those wires is different depending on which kind of amino acid is there, and so the equipment makes it possible to tell them apart by counting the molecules as they pass. [...] “By combining our nanogap tunneling technique with artificial intelligence, we were able to distinguish between the L- and D-forms of amino acids with over 80 per cent accuracy,” said lead author, Takahito Oshiro. “This is the first discrimination of amino-acid chirality at the single-molecule level and constitutes a fundamental advance in chemical sensing.”

title: Intel GPU D-Series Turns Crescent Island Into A 1.3 PFLOPS AI Beast
body: This launch comes as Intel attempts to establish a more competitive position in AI acceleration following its previous Gaudi efforts that were well-regarded but not very popular. Where previous-generation AI compute hardware was often focused on model training, this newer generation often focuses specifically on serving inference, as demand for inference is reportedly exploding. So it goes that the D-Series targets inference workloads, where memory capacity, serving efficiency, and the cost of [...] Intel has officially revealed the final form of Crescent Island, which turns out to be branded the "Intel GPU D-Series." The company's latest attempt to carve out a place in the data center AI accelerator market is led by the Intel GPU D270. This is a powerful inference-focused accelerator built around the new Xe3P architecture, supposedly the 'full' version of the Xe3 architecture that debuted with Panther Lake. The card combines up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory with 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 compute in [...] Intel says customer sampling is already underway and that it is working with OEMs, ODMs, cloud providers, and software partners to bring the hardware to market. Pricing and general availability have not yet been announced; obviously, we'll need third-party benchmarks to see how Intel's specs and claims hold up against real workloads.

title: Nvidia debuts three new open AI models
body:
Open models are less expensive to use, giving more organizations the option to use AI services. And the more companies that use AI, the more chips Nvidia can sell in the long run.

The company's newest models — Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, and Nemotron Bolt E4B 4GB — are designed to run AI agents on everything from data center systems to desktop computers. [...] Super VL is meant to power agents running across tasks that can take several days or weeks, Nvidia explained in a release. The company says that enterprises can also post-train the model on their own data, better customizing it for their exact needs.

While open-weight models generally trail closed models in terms of frontier capabilities, most users don't need such intense firepower for the jobs they need to accomplish. What's more, if a company can run open-weight models on its own hardware, they're more or less free to use.
